redox-reaction.context: Two circles for atoms with a curved arrow carrying an electron from one to the other. Used for chemistry lessons on oxidation and reduction and electron transfer diagrams.

dissolving.context: A glass of water with a sugar cube at the bottom and small particles drifting off it. Used for solubility lessons, kitchen science and solution chemistry.

sublimation.context: A solid block with wavy vapor lines rising straight up from its top. Used for phase change charts, dry ice demos and chemistry notes on solid to gas change.

chain-reaction.context: A branching tree where one circle splits into two and each of those releases small particles. Used for nuclear fission topics and cascade explanations.

isotope.context: Three columns of squares, each column taller than the last, above a baseline arrow. Used for chemistry and nuclear physics lessons about atoms of one element with different neutron counts.

radioactive-decay.context: A nucleus ringed with dots sending a small particle along a short line, with a wavy ray underneath. Used for radioactivity lessons, half life charts and nuclear safety topics.

radiation-penetration.context: Three arrows aimed at a thin sheet, a plate and a thick block, each stopping at a different barrier. Used for alpha, beta and gamma shielding diagrams and radiation safety.

atomic-orbital.context: Two teardrop lobes meeting at a point on a horizontal axis, shaped like a figure eight. Used for quantum chemistry, electron cloud diagrams and p orbital teaching.

galvanic-cell.context: Two small containers with metal strips joined by a wire through a round meter at the top. Used for electrochemistry lessons on batteries and voltaic cells.

corrosion.context: A metal bolt with ragged eaten edges and small flakes falling from it. Used for rust, metal decay and maintenance topics.

oil-and-water.context: A glass holding two separate layers with a few drops between them. Used for density, immiscible liquids and kitchen science explanations.

energy-levels.context: Stacked horizontal lines with an electron dot above them and a wavy photon leaving to the right. Used for Bohr model and emission diagrams in physics and chemistry.

plum-pudding-model.context: A large circle with small minus signs spread evenly inside. Used for atomic history timelines and the Thomson model of the atom.

phase-diagram.context: A graph with three regions split by curved lines that meet at a single point. Used for states of matter, pressure and temperature charts in chemistry.

boiling-point.context: A small pot with bubbles above it beside a tall thermometer. Used for cooking temperature notes and lessons on water boiling at 100 degrees.

freezing-point.context: A thermometer showing a low level beside an ice cube. Used for cold weather, melting and freezing point lessons.

light-polarization.context: A wavy line entering a slotted filter and leaving as a flatter wave. Used for optics lessons, polarized lens topics and light wave diagrams.

optical-fiber.context: Two curved lines forming a glass strand with dots showing a light ray bouncing inside. Used for networking, internet cable and total internal reflection topics.

concave-mirror.context: A curved mirror arc with two parallel rays bouncing off to meet at one point. Used for ray diagrams in optics and focal length lessons.

standing-wave.context: Two mirrored wave curves fixed at both ends with dots at the still points. Used for string vibration, resonance and harmonics in physics and music.

optical-bench.context: A long rail with a candle at one end, a lens in the middle and a screen at the other end. Used for physics lab experiments on lenses and image formation.

light-dispersion.context: A beam entering a triangular prism and fanning out into separate rays. Used for rainbow, spectrum and refraction lessons.

airfoil-lift.context: A wing cross-section with curved air lines passing over and under it. Used for aerodynamics, flight and Bernoulli principle explanations.

laser-interferometer.context: Two long arms at a right angle with a block at the corner and mirrors at the ends. Used for gravitational wave detection and precision measurement topics.

heat-conduction.context: A metal rod with a small flame at one end and heat wisps rising along its length. Used for thermal conduction and heat transfer lessons.

elastic-collision.context: Two balls touching with spark lines above and arrows pointing apart below. Used for momentum, impact and billiard physics lessons.

centripetal-force.context: A ball on a round path with an arrow pulling inward toward the center. Used for circular motion and orbit diagrams in physics.

potential-energy.context: A ball sitting on a raised block with an arrow showing the drop to the ground. Used for gravity and stored energy lessons.

electroscope.context: A jar with a rod through the top ending in a ball and two thin leaves that spread apart. Used for static electricity experiments and charge detection.

electromagnetic-induction.context: A bar magnet moving toward a wire coil that connects to a small meter. Used for Faraday law lessons, generators and transformers.

damped-oscillation.context: A wave that starts tall and shrinks step by step toward a flat line. Used for vibration, spring and signal decay graphs.

magnetic-repulsion.context: Two bar magnets facing each other with arrows pointing outward below them. Used for magnetism lessons on like poles pushing apart.

cyclotron.context: Two D-shaped halves facing each other with a spiral path starting at the center. Used for particle accelerator and nuclear medicine topics.

cloud-chamber.context: A box tank with a dark base and thin particle trails crossing inside. Used for particle detection and radiation demonstrations.

ferrofluid.context: A spiky blob of liquid standing up in points above a flat magnet. Used for magnetism demonstrations and science museum exhibits.

string-telephone.context: Two cups joined by a taut string with small sound arcs next to one cup. Used for sound, vibration and kids science activities.

tornado-bottle.context: Two bottles joined neck to neck with a funnel swirling in the upper one. Used for science fair projects and vortex demonstrations.

sand-filter.context: A funnel holding layered grit with clean drops falling from the spout. Used for water purification, filtration lessons and survival guides.

absorption-spectrum.context: A band crossed by a few thin dark lines above a short wavelength scale. Used for spectroscopy, astronomy and chemistry analysis.

blackbody-radiation.context: Axes with a curve that climbs to a peak and then falls. Used for thermal radiation, Planck law and quantum physics history.

photoelectric-effect.context: Wavy light heading down toward a metal plate while a small electron flies off it. Used for quantum physics and solar cell topics.

bloch-sphere.context: A sphere with an equator ring and an arrow from the center to the surface. Used for quantum computing and qubit state diagrams.

cosmic-ray-shower.context: One track from the top that splits into a widening spread of particle tracks. Used for particle physics and astronomy detector topics.

antimatter.context: A particle with a plus beside a particle with a minus and a small spark above them. Used for particle physics and science fiction themes.

vector-addition.context: Two arrows placed tip to tail with a third arrow closing a triangle. Used for physics force diagrams and math vector lessons.

free-fall.context: A large ball and a small ball falling side by side with short speed lines above and a ground line. Used for gravity and acceleration lessons.

beam-splitter.context: A glass cube with a diagonal mirror, one beam entering and two beams leaving. Used for optics and laser experiment setups.

chladni-plate.context: A square plate on a central post with a diamond pattern traced by sand. Used for acoustics, vibration and sound visualization.

turbulent-flow.context: Straight flow lines meeting a round obstacle and breaking into curls behind it. Used for fluid dynamics and aerodynamics.

surface-tension.context: A small paperclip resting on a water line that dips beneath it. Used for liquid physics and water properties lessons.

viscosity.context: Two pouring edges, one with a long thick drip and one with small fast drops. Used for fluid thickness, honey and oil comparisons.

fluid-pressure.context: A tall container with three jets of water curving out and reaching farther from the lower holes. Used for hydrostatic pressure lessons.

ribosome.context: A small oval sitting on a larger oval above a thin wavy strand. Used for cell biology and protein synthesis diagrams.

meiosis.context: One circle splitting into two circles that lead to four smaller dots. Used for biology lessons on cell division and gamete formation.

dna-sequence.context: A horizontal strip of four cells with small marks above and below. Used for genome sequencing and genetic code topics.

dna-fingerprint.context: A square gel with three lanes of short bars at different heights. Used for forensic DNA profiling and electrophoresis results.

transfer-rna.context: A cloverleaf of three rings around a short stem with an open end at the top. Used for molecular biology and protein translation diagrams.

action-potential.context: Axes with a smooth spike that rises sharply, dips below rest and returns. Used for neuroscience and nerve signal charts.

transpiration.context: A plant with an arrow rising beside it and wavy vapor leaving the leaves. Used for botany lessons on how water moves through plants.

phagocytosis.context: A large round cell with two arms curling around a small rod-shaped bacterium. Used for immune system and cell biology teaching.

coccolithophore.context: A round alga made of overlapping button-like plates with a dot in each. Used for marine biology and ocean carbon topics.

desmid.context: A single-celled alga shaped like two joined lobes pinched at the waist. Used for pond life, microscopy and freshwater biology.

bacteria-shapes.context: Three microbes side by side, round cocci, a rod and a corkscrew. Used for microbiology lessons on bacterial types.

chlamydomonas.context: A round green alga with two whip tails at the top and a small eyespot inside. Used for biology lessons on single-celled swimmers.

cyanobacteria.context: A curling chain of small beaded squares forming a filament. Used for algal bloom and microbe topics.

trypanosome.context: A slim wavy cell with a ruffled fin along one side and a whip at the front. Used for parasitology and tropical disease teaching.

penicillium-mold.context: A stalk ending in a brush of branches tipped with chains of round spores. Used for fungus, antibiotic history and food mold topics.

nematode.context: A slender worm curving in an S shape inside a round microscope field. Used for soil biology, parasite and lab slide topics.

pitfall-trap.context: A cup sunk into the ground with its rim level with the soil and a raised cover above it. Used for insect surveys and ecology fieldwork.

mist-net.context: A fine net strung between two poles with a small bird caught in it. Used for bird ringing, ornithology fieldwork and wildlife surveys.

bat-detector.context: A handheld box with a small speaker and dial below a flying bat. Used for bat surveys and ultrasound recording in ecology.

telemetry-antenna.context: A handheld directional antenna with crossbars on a boom and a small receiver box. Used for radio tracking of tagged animals.

plaster-track-cast.context: A round plaster cast with a raised animal paw print on it. Used for wildlife tracking, nature crafts and field guides.

population-growth-curve.context: Axes with an S-shaped curve that levels off under a dashed limit line. Used for ecology and logistic growth charts.

predator-prey-cycle.context: Axes with two offset waves where one trails the other. Used for ecology charts on population cycles.

stellar-wobble.context: A planet dot on a large circle with a small ring and star dot at the center. Used for exoplanet detection and astronomy teaching.

elliptical-orbit.context: An oval path with a small sun near one end and a planet dot on the path. Used for Kepler laws and solar system diagrams.
